english_verification.review_scope: Checked the current Mod's Z17 opening history, English Z17/Z74 names, the formation mission and representative mission/flavour terminology; read the actual Obrtrol origins chunk and the related post-1444 polity chunk. This was not a full mission, event, or balance audit, and native English national ideas were not retranscribed. Native English national-idea names and descriptions were compared by localisation key by the primary. Large source intervals are locator envelopes, not a claim to inspect every intervening line or establish complete runtime reachability.
unresolved: The Obrtrol Wiki page presents Frost-Giant origin as disputed and contains contradictory ancient chronology; no precise ancient year was used.
The related polity page does not establish a unique formation year or current formation mechanics; local missions remain authoritative.
Opening tactics, end-state timing, and blessing values were not playtested or exhaustively audited.

rationale.campaign_length: The structured database identifies 25 shared Z17/Z74 missions and 30 Z74 follow-up missions.
rationale.colonization: Northern roads and remote-area exploration require development; this is not an ocean-colonial country.
rationale.complexity: War order, construction and development gates, population events, and post-formation missions run together.
rationale.dark_story: Captured slave labour, permanent slave mines, and the destruction of Dwarven holds are explicit dark aspects of the current route.
rationale.difficulty: Opening wars and later regional-prosperity and university requirements are demanding; this has not been playtested.
rationale.diplomacy: There are political choices involving grey orcs and ogres, but military integration remains the main means of progress.
rationale.early_pressure: Northern isolation, a weak economy, and strong southern human neighbours create high pressure; a fixed declaration date is unverified.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Runes, shamans, mage towers, and mountain blessings strengthen the middle and late game, but Troll armies remain central.
rationale.narrative_density: Ancestral legend, restoration, the Z17-to-Z74 transition, kin integration, and Dwarven enemies form a continuous story.
rationale.tall_play: The capital, ancient forge, giant palaces, regional prosperity, and public schools all require construction.
rationale.trade_economy: The ancient forge, mining, and regional prosperity provide an economic layer; trade is not the main loop.
rationale.warfare: Breaking the human neighbours, unifying Gerudia, pushing north, and fighting Dwarven holds run through the campaign.

identity.appearance: A nine-province Fjord Troll settled tribe in 1444 that can become Z74 Gerudaghot after its unique missions are completed.
identity.formation_scope: The Z17-specific mission obrtrol_geruds_legacy_seized changes the country to Z74 after the related branches, peace, and control of 995 and 985; if Z74 already exists, it gives money only.

successors.relationship: A normal mission-formed successor that changes to monarchy, adds a government reform and non-generic missions, carries 25 shared Z17/Z74 missions, and unlocks 30 Z74-specific missions.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

Maybe is time for Trolls to wear human clothing, at least the ones with the shiny objects on them, and the furry ones.

description.text: The destruction of the humans has restored the order that once ruled everything. The natural order that saw it fit for giants to rule is back and here to stay, with the leftover tracks of Gerudian farmland becoming good eating for the mammoths that once roamed the land. The news of their return has spread across the continent, and has piqued the interest of puny humans looking to buy furs and tusks only we can provide.

description.text: The mines of Dalrfjäll are of extreme importance to our new empire and our future plans. These caves are worked by humans, meatbags slaving away in the mines to earn their right to eat and sleep, providing us with the materials we need to continue our wars while they get our protection. But recently we've heard reports of humans becoming overstressed and rather... unsavory. Because of this, we changed the system of labor used in the mines, providing the wimpy little meatbags with proper schedules of work, ensuring they work good and grumble less.

description.text: Gerud was the Frost Giant that ruled over the land eleven thousand years ago. The frost giants made us to protect them against any outsiders who dare approach the cold towers of the north. Every man, woman and child of Gerudaghot knows that defending the north is what we must do. By marking our warriors with the runes of the frost king we can remind them that we are the chosen ones that will protect the north until the end of days!

description.text: The world operates under a simple principle: the big rule over the small, and the small suck it up and do what we say. Problem is, the puny humans and their stinky allies found ways to turn our weaknesses against us, disrupting the natural balance of the world. Even now, as we rule over a land gained through our superiority, there are still those dumb enough to challenge our right to rule over them like the bugs they are. The discovery of the frost towers left by the giants here millennia ago have proven our beliefs beyond any shadow of a doubt, and has given us a greater, more concrete mandate that We are the Giant's chosen!

description.text: The cold cannot hurt a troll, neither can the swords or sledgehammers of the dumb soldiers we've faced over the years. But with time the secret of our weakness to fire and acid became widespread, especially in this era of black powder and cannonballs. By calling on the power of the runes, we can bring the freezing cold with us and have our armies wear it like a moving blizzard, freezing bullets and turning any warriors willing to fight us into tasty meatsicles.

description.text: Nothing is more legendary than the hunger of us trolls, whether it be the smallest troll child or the greatest of warchiefs, our love of a good meal is universal, and it shows in our recipes. Our contact with other races has greatly expanded our culinary palate, and we appreciate their contributions in the expansion of troll culinary culture, whether it be in stews, mashes, or puddings. With choices like these, no troll in our empire will be left wanting!

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid this if you do not want early defensive wars, later prosperity and university gates, or a narrative involving slave labour and destroyed cities.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Defend in the mountains, integrate the tribes, and contest Gerudia early; repair the ancient giant sites and form Z74 in the middle game; develop the whole region, train mammoths, push north, and pursue the giant inheritance later.
player_overview.overview: Obrtrol is a Fjord Troll tribe trapped at the northern end of Gerudia in 1444. Use its strong Troll army to survive human neighbours, reclaim the ancient forge, repair the capital, and integrate the Trolls; the restoration mission turns it into Gerudaghot and opens the mammoth, rune, holy-site, and northern-empire second half. It is a hard opening followed by a long restoration campaign, but slave mines and the destruction of Dwarven holds give the victory a clear dark cost.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy high-pressure openings, heavy Troll armies, ancient giant ruins, and long northern-empire campaigns.
signature_features: A nine-province Troll tribe becomes Gerudaghot through missions, with its government and later missions changing together.
Ancient giant forges, palaces, runes, and Mountain Watcher blessings support the northern restoration.
Mammoths and strong Troll armies drive expansion, while the late empire combines public works, kin integration, and slave oppression.
player_overview.tagline: Lead the northern Trolls back to their homeland and reforge the ancient giants' ruins into an empire.

reasons: Formation changes the government, ideas, and missions together
Mammoths, runes, holy sites, and ancient giant relics create a distinctive fantasy
warnings: Human neighbours create extreme defensive pressure at the start
Late prosperity and university gates are slow
Slave labour and destroyed Dwarven cities are not a purely positive restoration story

phase_scores.phase: Tribal survival and existing human oppression
Institutional slave mines and destroyed Dwarven holds

positive_indicators: Events allow grey-orc culture to be accepted and tolerance to be raised
Ogre kin can be aided with homelands and generous taxation
Missions promote Gerudian prosperity and public schools
values.rationale: Restoration, monarchy, and war are not penalized by themselves. The capital already has an oppressed human minority; mission text depicts captured slave labour, post-formation scripts establish permanent slave mines and lower human tolerance, and late missions deliberately damage four Dwarven holds. Gerudian prosperity, public schools, optional grey-orc acceptance, and aid to ogres add public benefit and limited recognition of personhood, but do not cancel institutional harm to humans and Dwarves.
red_flags: The capital province history contains an oppressed human minority
Missions and narrative arrange captured slave labour and permanent slave mines
Four Dwarven holds are deliberately reduced, devastated, and left permanently damaged late in the route
